label: Type B to Type C design replacement boundary
notes: Direct photographed 1746 copy is Type B; archived 1747 frontispiece thumbnail is structurally Type C; 1748 institutional scan is Type C. The design-level replacement boundary is fixed at 1746/1747.

label: Does late Type A recurrence represent the same physical matrix?
notes: Type A is directly controlled in the 1720s–1730s and reappears in 1759 and 1765 after Types B and C have circulated. This establishes repertoire/stock recurrence at design level, not one copperplate across four decades. Frozen 2026-08-30 at the high-resolution pairwise matrix-test boundary; the unresolved physical identity is preserved rather than inferred.
reopen_rule: Compare dimensions, plate marks, lettering, stable scratches/defects, wear and retouching across at least one early Type A impression and the 1759/1765 late impressions. No further design-level search is authorized.

label: Type C matrix/state sequence and the fec. 1755 problem
notes: Type C is directly present by 1747 and in 1748, 1749, 1751, 1755, two 1756 copies, 1757, 1761 and 1763. Finna reads M. Turoff fec. 1755 on the 1762 frontispiece. The date is a within-Type-C matrix/state problem, not an invention date for the design. Frozen 2026-08-30 as a bounded high-resolution copy-pair refinement.
reopen_rule: Obtain high-resolution, copy-paired images for 1751/1755/1761/1762/1763 and compare production line, frame, lettering, dimensions and stable defects. Reopen only if a publication argument requires physical matrix-state chronology.

label: Late Seyfart/Raspe frontispiece persistence and copy divergence, 1767–1776
notes: Catalogue controls show copy-dependent late configurations: some multi-volume sets report repeated frontispieces, some collations do not count one, and a 1771 volume has a Titelkupfer. A ca.1773 market object may be a Clio-bearing Handbuch but host identification is unconfirmed. reopen_rule: Inspect opening leaves of at least one secure 1767/1768 copy and targeted 1773 BSB Handbuch bsb10428164 only if late copy-level persistence becomes necessary to the final argument. Do not recreate generic search tasks.

label: Publisher stock custody from Weigel through Tyroff and into later host regimes
notes: The 1766 Verlagskupfer preface directly proves a Weigel/Tyroff publishing environment in which old coppers were retained as publisher-held reusable capital. Firm succession makes long-lived plate stock plausible, but direct custody of the Historia/Genealogia/Heraldica matrices across specific owners remains unproved. Frozen 2026-08-30 at the archival/account/inventory boundary; the probable status is intentionally retained.
reopen_rule: Require dated firm/estate/account/inventory evidence or matrix-level physical continuity linking the frontispiece stock. Do not infer custody solely from design recurrence or family succession.

label: Issue-level resolution of C. Weigels Witwe
notes: Current firm-succession evidence favours Magdalena Esther Weigel for the elder-Weigel Wappenkalender imprint, while some catalogues assign 1731–1735 records to Barbara Magdalena Weigel. Literal imprint and person resolution remain separate. Frozen 2026-08-30 at the issue-level archival/title-page boundary; no unsupported person-level promotion is made.
reopen_rule: Only direct title-page, privilege, advertisement, account, or contemporary firm evidence tying a specific issue to one household should change the issue-level person resolution.

label: Final historiographical novelty boundary
notes: Final sweep completed 2026-08-27. Generic claims about epistemic frontispieces, visual/material evidence, century-scale prototype reuse, context-dependent reuse, plate custody/repair/reprinting, copy remaking and Göttingen material evidence are prior art. The defensible gap is the specific programme/design/matrix/state/witness/copy history of the Nürnberg serial apparatus and its selective rehosting/re-specification in the Gatterer/Göttingen environment.
reopen_rule: Reopen only for newly published scholarship or a newly identified study directly on the Weigel/Köhler/Gatterer/Raspe ecology, the Historia Genealogia Heraldica lineage, or the specific Nürnberg-to-Göttingen transfer/re-specification mechanism.
